items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.snippet: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.

items.title: Stripe backer Atomico calls for Europe to own its success stories

items.title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang's ouster

items.title: Nvidia says it doesn't plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO

items.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO

items.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit

items.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it's not having one
items.snippet: With tech outages seemingly everywhere, Google took the unusual step of announcing that Gmail is working just fine, actually.

items.title: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order

items.title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?

items.snippet: The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.

By all accounts, Apple squandered its early lead in the podcasting game. The iPod, the Apple device that revolutionized the music industry in the early 2000s, made it possible to carry audio around for easy listening, and clever third-party software made it simple to transfer so-called audioblogs to the digital music player. (Apple added podcasts to iTunes 4.9 in June 2005, a year after journalist Ben Hammersley proposed the term “podcasting” in an article in The Guardian). items.title: Today in Apple history: Apple's last mechanical keyboard is a winner
items.snippet: November 15, 1990: Cupertino wins a design patent for the Apple Extended Keyboard II, arguably the greatest computer keyboard of all time. Delivering the perfect combination of durability, feel and a pleasing click-clack sound, the Extended Keyboard II will become a mainstay of pro-grade Apple setups during the early 1990s — and perhaps the best-loved keyboard in Apple history. Courtesy of an ADB-to-USB adapter, some people continue to use these input devices today. In an era when Apple typically obsesses over making everything thinner, lighter and more minimalist, the Extended Keyboard II stands as a glorious reminder that sometimes bigger really is better. This hulking mechanical keyboard delivered something today’s sleek accessories often sacrifice: a deeply satisfying typing experience. Its spring-loaded Alps switches, crisp click-clack sound and thoughtful ergonomic touches made it a cult favorite that some Mac users still refuse to give up. The original Extended Keyboard arrived in 1987, after Steve Jobs left Apple following his battle with CEO John Sculley. In the same way th…

items.title: macOS 27.3’s new Full Disk Access prompt protects your data from apps that want it
items.snippet: Macworld In October, Apple announced that it was going to change how it implements Full Disk Access control in macOS. Users were going to have to perform “very explicit user action” to grant FDA to an app, which is a change from before, when apps could prompt users to flip switches on in System Settings to allow FDA. The change is coming to macOS 27.3, and it was recently unveiled in the macOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday. Apple released a note to developers notifying them about the change, stating that the changes “empower [users] to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.” The new FDA UI was posted online by madeby_ldt, and it’s much more detailed and explicit.

items.snippet: Macworld Apple HomeView is Apple’s first dedicated smart-home display, combining a 7-inch touchscreen, powerful speakers, a camera, and Siri AI in a device designed to sit at the center of the connected home. items.title: Apple, please bring that new iPhone Duo feature to my MacBook
items.snippet: Macworld With the iOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday, Apple unveiled a cool new feature for iPhone Duo users. I don’t own a Duo, but it’s such a cool feature I’m really hoping Apple brings it to the MacBook. One of the iPhone Duo’s biggest flaws is that the front camera doesn’t have Face ID and instead relies on Touch ID for unlocking. But in the iOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple provided a surprisingly clever workaround. The front camera will be able to be used to unlock the iPhone Duo if the phone had performed a Touch ID or password authentication in the past 45 minutes. It’s not true Face ID, but it’s a handy workaroud that considers both security and convenience. Essentially, Apple ported

items.title: iPhone Duo 2 rumored to get Face ID, but other upgrades will need to wait
items.snippet: Macworld Mark Gurman’s latest Power On newsletter is mostly about Apple’s upcoming smart glasses, but it does have one interesting bit of iPhone Duo 2 information in it. Apple has been aware that the missing Face ID is an issue since before the device launched, and has been working on adding it to the second-gen version. According to Gurman, the company has iPhone Duo 2 with Face ID in prototype form, but the design is not finalized. items.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: What’s new, what’s in the beta & what’s next
items.snippet: Macworld macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, introducing an all-new Siri AI assistant, major updates to Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, and expanded child-safety features. Design refinements and performance improvements round out the release. Named after California’s iconic Golden Gate, the update continues Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, bringing Apple Intelligence to more parts of the operating system to help users complete everyday tasks faster. macOS 27 supports all Macs powered by Apple silicon, but drops support for Intel-based models. items.snippet: Macworld Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. The latest update, iOS 27.2.1 arrived on November 9, with security fixes. items.snippet: Every to-do list runs forever. Ivy runs for a day. Each morning you turn ideas into a plan. Each evening, whatever’s left is an idea again. Nothing is overdue. Tomorrow starts empty. We built a prototype and couldn’t stop using it. Beneath the calm: Calendar and Reminders integration, focus sessions, Screen Time shields, and a daily journal. All native: SwiftUI, UIKit, Metal. Ivy is on iPhone , with Mac to follow. Let me know what you think! ★

items.title: ‘Unlock With Front Camera’ — New Feature for iPhone Duo in iOS 27.3 Beta 2
items.snippet: Juli Clover, MacRumors: Apple today added a new option for unlocking the iPhone Duo using the front-facing camera, giving device users multiple ways to access their content. The feature is available in the second iOS 27.3 beta. The option to unlock with facial recognition is only available on the Lock Screen, and authentication via Touch ID is still needed for Apple Pay purchases, adding passwords and logins, and more. Unlocking with the camera requires a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, and Touch ID is required again after about 45 minutes of inactivity. items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before a House Foreign Affairs panel amid concerns over his affair with a suspected Chinese spy

The appearances follow Huang's admission of an affair with a woman who worked for an Nvidia customer who is also believed to be a Chinese spy.

items.title: Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang

Another affair, this time with an employee, has since been reported.

items.title: AMD attacks Nvidia's FP64 emulation at SC26, touts native double-precision on Instinct MI430X
